title: The Growth Kinetic and Ultra High Hardness of CoCrFeNiTi High–Entropy Alloy by Mechanical Alloying and Spark Plasma Sintering

recollection.starting_material: Likely elemental powders of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti
recollection.intervention: Mechanical alloying to produce a nanocrystalline high-entropy alloy powder, followed by consolidation with spark plasma sintering
recollection.structure: Probably a single-phase or dual-phase FCC/BCC nanocrystalline CoCrFeNiTi solid solution with very fine grain size
recollection.mechanism: Severe plastic deformation during milling leads to solid-solution formation; rapid SPS heating limits grain growth, preserving nanostructure and solution strengthening; possibly precipitation of Ti-rich phases that further strengthen the matrix
recollection.results: I would guess reported Vickers hardness above 1000 HV and perhaps compressive yield strength above 2 GPa, attributed to the retained nanocrystallinity and multi-element solid-solution strengthening, but this is only a conjecture.

score.note: The intervention is only the generic mechanical-alloying/SPS sequence already evident from the title, without milling or sintering conditions. The recollection correctly identifies a nanocrystalline mixed FCC/BCC solid solution and gives substantially correct strengthening mechanisms, although Ti-rich precipitation is speculative. The guessed hardness and yield strength are far above the actual 675 HV and 1238 MPa.
